clue.text: One should be critical about Gogglebox participant?

parts.note: re is the Latin-derived word for 'concerning'
Gogglebox is a British TV show in which members of the public are filmed watching television, so its participants are people who watch

explanation.surface: A question about whether someone on a reality TV sofa should be judging what they watch.
explanation.walkthrough: Gogglebox is a British programme filming ordinary households as they watch and comment on TV.
explanation.definitionFit: A critic who assesses books, films or shows is someone whose job is to be critical.

clue.text: Bores worry about liberation South supports

indicators.note: in a down entry the letter below holds up what is above it, so the South letter goes at the bottom
worry wraps itself about the short form of liberation, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: to worry is to care, to be concerned
Lib is the familiar short form, as in Women's Lib
S is the compass abbreviation for South

explanation.surface: Tedious people fret about freedom while the southern states back them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bores' looks like a plural noun for dull people; here it means the internal diameters of gun barrels.
explanation.definitionFit: The bore of a gun barrel is its internal diameter, also called its calibre, so the plural matches.

clue.text: Suppress a stench that's spread

indicators.note: a smell that has spread has dispersed and broken apart, so these letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to contain a bad smell before it travels further.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's spread' turns the letters of A STENCH into a new arrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: To chasten is to subdue or restrain, a sense close to suppressing someone's pride or spirit.

clue.text: Freelance journalist with no sign of hesitation following thread

indicators.note: having no part of something means that part is taken away from the rest

parts.note: a stringer is a journalist paid per piece rather than kept on staff
er is the sound people make while hesitating

explanation.surface: A confident freelance reporter follows a line of inquiry without stumbling.
explanation.walkthrough: A stringer is a freelance paid per story; 'with no' strips the hesitant sound, and 'following' is only a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A thread and a cord are both a thin length of twisted fibre, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Ha'pence for change caught out object of extravagant courtship

indicators.note: an old coin offered for change suggests its letters are changed into a new order
something left out is removed, so this letter drops away from the rest

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught on a scorecard

explanation.surface: An old halfpenny coin handed over as change, with someone caught out in the transaction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes C from HAPENCE, giving HAPENE, which 'for change' rearranges. A ha'penny was an old British halfpenny coin.
explanation.definitionFit: The female peafowl is the bird the peacock courts by fanning out his lavish tail display.

clue.text: Rump of goat but no duck in hearty red hot meat tapas dished up for un-birthday bash

indicators.note: food dished up is served out, here meaning the letters are reworked into a new order
the rump is the hind end, so the final letter is taken
having no duck means that letter is removed from the pool

parts.note: a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so it stands for the letter O

explanation.surface: A spicy meat tapas spread, minus the duck and with a bit of goat, served up for a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rump of' gives T from goat; 'but no' removes the O (a duck is zero) from HEARTY RED HOT MEAT TAPAS; 'dished up' rearranges the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: In Alice in Wonderland the guests at this riotous gathering celebrate an un-birthday, every day that is not one's birthday.

clue.text: See 19
Would-be personality exchanged views with bishop dismissed for empty stalls

parts.note: one's self is one's whole personality or individual nature

indicators.note: one item is sent away in favour of another, so a replacement is made

parts.note: people who have conferred have discussed things together
RR, Right Reverend, is the title of a bishop

indicators.note: an emptied word keeps only its outer letters

explanation.surface: A character swapped opinions with a bishop who was thrown out in favour of empty choir seats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dismissed for' swaps RR (Right Reverend, a bishop's title) in CONFERRED for SS, which 'empty' leaves of 'stalls'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe someone who claims a status by their own admission, as in a self-styled or aspiring expert.

clue.text: Infamous atoll's sparse cover?

definitions.meaning: a Pacific atoll in the Marshall Islands used for US nuclear bomb tests
a skimpy two-piece swimsuit that covers very little

explanation.surface: A notorious Pacific island has only thin vegetation covering it.
explanation.definitionFit: The two-piece swimsuit was named after the atoll, the site of US atomic tests in 1946.

clue.text: Sylvester Stallone shortly to tackle Shaft? Quite!

indicators.note: to tackle something is to take it on, here to wrap round it

parts.note: the actor's nickname is a short form of his first name, Sly
a shaft of sunshine is a beam of light

explanation.surface: Asks whether the actor Stallone should take on the role of the private detective Shaft.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage 'quite' often means 'somewhat' or 'a little', not 'completely'.
explanation.definitionFit: British 'quite', as in 'quite cold', means somewhat or to a small degree, a mild intensifier.

clue.text: See 19
Run through gardens in South East by river

indicators.note: the gardens sit inside the abbreviation for the region

parts.note: SE is the compass abbreviation for South East
Kew Gardens are the Royal Botanic Gardens in south-west London
R is the abbreviation for river on maps

explanation.surface: A jogging route that passes through gardens in the south-east of England by a river.
explanation.walkthrough: Kew Gardens are London's Royal Botanic Gardens, by the Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: To pierce something right through, as with a pointed rod or sword, is the verb sense meant here.

clue.text: Stock improvement from genius involved with Eric Clapton initially

indicators.note: something involved is intricate and tangled, so the letters are mixed together
the opening letters of the two words are taken

explanation.surface: A guitar hero's genius is credited with boosting the market.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives E and C from Eric Clapton; 'involved' rearranges them with GENIUS. 'Stock' means breeding lines, not shares.
explanation.definitionFit: The discredited science of selective breeding aimed to improve the human gene pool, the stock of a population.

clue.text: Slippery character list announced in EastEnders?

indicators.note: EastEnders is a soap set in London's East End, where Cockneys drop the opening H when speaking

parts.note: a ship that lists, or tilts, is said to heel over

explanation.surface: A shifty character from a TV soap reads out a list.
explanation.walkthrough: EastEnders is a BBC soap set in East London, where the Cockney accent drops the initial H.
explanation.definitionFit: A wriggling fish that is hard to grip; the word is also used for an evasive, untrustworthy person.

clue.text: Dowager Dame Myra or Deputy Führer Rudolf suppressing rage

indicators.note: holding something down means it is kept inside the other piece

parts.words: Dame Myra or Deputy Führer Rudolf
parts.note: both share the surname Hess: the pianist Dame Myra and Hitler's deputy Rudolf
ire is anger or rage

explanation.surface: Two famous people with the same surname, a pianist and a Nazi, are contrasted.
explanation.walkthrough: The long middle stretch is one piece: both people named share the surname HESS.
explanation.definitionFit: A dowager is a widow holding property or title inherited from her late husband, so loosely a woman who has inherited.

clue.text: Close border?

definitions.meaning: the close is the finish or conclusion
a border is an edge or extremity

explanation.surface: Is that frontier nearby?
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a conclusion and the outer limit or edge of something.

clue.text: Dried meat left in small piece not quite gone off

indicators.note: the letter for left sits inside the word for a small piece

parts.note: a bit is a small piece

indicators.note: meat gone off has turned bad, so these letters are spoiled into a new order
not quite the whole word, so the last letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A piece of dried meat has been left too long and is going bad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite' drops E from GONE; 'off' rearranges GON to ONG.
explanation.definitionFit: A South African speciality of salted, air-cured strips of meat, much like jerky.

clue.text: Sounds like science of identification, reads like freshwater fish science, but is an entire way of thinking

parts.note: the ide is a European freshwater fish of the carp family
an -ology is a branch of knowledge or science

explanation.surface: A word game: one subject sounds like identification studies, reads like fish science, and is a worldview.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening stretch is a bonus flourish: said aloud the word suggests ID-ology, a study of identification. The charade is the written reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A system of ideas and beliefs that shapes a group's whole outlook, such as a political creed.

clue.text: See 6
Krays perhaps surrounding rickety Elk Lake billet (misprinted, Times admitted) — nonsense from 6 Across 18 Down

indicators.note: the pair of twins each wrap round the jumbled letters

parts.note: the Krays were notorious London gangster twins, so two of them suggest twin and twin

indicators.note: something rickety is shaky and badly put together, so the letters are jumbled
a misprinted text has its letters out of order, so these are rearranged

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time, and two of them give the plural

explanation.surface: Gangster twins around a shaky lakeside billet, with a misprint and a newspaper admission, from Alice.
explanation.walkthrough: The Kray twins were 1960s London gangsters. Each TWIN 'surrounding' KLE ('rickety' Elk), then 'misprinted' rearranges LAKE BILLET with TT 'admitted'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mad Hatter recites this parody of a nursery rhyme at the tea party in Alice's Adventures in Wonderland.

clue.text: Recall wife hit out against lottery

indicators.note: out here means wild or off course, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a draw is a lottery or raffle

explanation.surface: A husband recalls how his wife lashed out against the lottery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges HIT to ITH.
explanation.definitionFit: To recall something, such as a product or an ambassador, is to take it back or pull it out.

clue.text: Silver lining in showing respect

indicators.note: the silver forms a lining inside the other word

parts.note: to be home is to be in
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A play on the proverb that every cloud has a silver lining, recast as respect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Silver lining' looks like a set phrase but splits: silver is the chemical symbol and 'lining' places it within the word for 'in', as in being at home.
explanation.definitionFit: Paying tribute is an act of showing deference and respect, as in to pay tribute to someone.

clue.text: Painter of plump pulchritude not having finished eating English salt beef sandwich

indicators.note: the shortened painter swallows the English letter
not finished means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: the Flemish painter Rubens was famous for voluptuous nudes

explanation.surface: A painter of fleshy beauties breaks off mid-meal to eat an English sandwich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not having finished' trims S from RUBENS; 'eating' puts E inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot American deli sandwich of corned beef, sauerkraut and Swiss cheese on rye bread.

clue.text: Delighted to have got on without introduction

indicators.note: without its introduction the word loses its first letter

parts.note: people who related to each other got on well

explanation.surface: Pleased to have become friends even without being introduced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without introduction' drops R from RELATED.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a state of great joy and high spirits, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Two short words promising one long commitment

definitions.text: Two short words promising one long commitment

parts.words: Two short words promising one long commitment
parts.note: the brief vow spoken by each partner at a wedding, pledging a lifelong marriage

explanation.surface: Two tiny words carry a lifetime's promise.
explanation.definitionFit: The vow said at the altar in a wedding service commits the speaker to marriage for life.

clue.text: New York baseball team possibly makes alpine move?

parts.note: the Mets are a New York baseball team; read the two-word answer as an instruction, turning its first word round, and it gives their name

explanation.surface: A baseball team could make a move in the Alps.
explanation.walkthrough: This works backwards: read the answer as an instruction, turn the first word round, and it spells METS, the New York Mets baseball team.
explanation.definitionFit: A skiing manoeuvre in which one ski is angled out to change direction, used on alpine slopes.

clue.text: Elvis, Ali asked regularly to work together

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals means every other one

explanation.surface: Elvis Presley and Muhammad Ali are invited to collaborate.
explanation.definitionFit: To liaise is to cooperate and keep in contact so that people coordinate their efforts.

clue.text: Leftie egghead last in line going for leader of Labour somehow soaring

indicators.note: done somehow means in some unknown way, so the letters are rearranged
one letter goes in favour of another, so a replacement is made
the final letter of the word is taken
the leader is the first letter

explanation.surface: A left-wing intellectual is ousted in favour of the Labour leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last in' line is E; 'going for' swaps an E for L ('leader of Labour'); 'somehow' rearranges the result. The word is in Chambers.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally flying high like the great bird of prey, so figuratively soaring or lofty in ambition.
